title: Untwisted integral classes form the dual Tate module
statement:
Let $C_0/k_0$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve,
let $C=C_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, and let $J$ be its
Jacobian, equipped with the canonical semilinear
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{k}_0/k_0)$-action of
[lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action]. Put
$A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. There is a natural Galois-equivariant
isomorphism

$$
\varprojlim_n H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C,A_n)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(T_\ell J,\mathbf Z_\ell).
\tag{4.1}
$$

Here $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and the inverse limit uses the
reduction maps in the coefficient system.
The Tate module and etale cohomology are those of
[def-wf-abelian-tate-module], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text:
Put $M_n=J[\ell^n](\overline{k}_0)$ and $U_n=H^1(C,A_n)$. Write $\kappa_n:H^1(C,A_n(1))\simeq M_n$ for [lem-wf-curve-kummer-jacobian-tate-module]. The perfect pairing of [lem-wf-curve-finite-level-pd] gives an $A_n$-linear isomorphism
$$\phi_n:U_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(M_n,A_n),\qquad
\phi_n(x)(y)=\operatorname{tr}_{C,n}(x\smile\kappa_n^{-1}y).$$
Indeed, perfectness means exactly that the adjoint into the dual of the second factor is bijective, and precomposition with $\kappa_n^{-1}$ is an isomorphism of the two duals. The curve is smooth projective and geometrically connected and $\ell$ is invertible, precisely as required by both cited statements.

source.place: Blueprint proof, equation (4.2) and construction of (4.3)

proof.text:
Use [lem-wf-curve-trace-cup-naturality] in degree $i=1$, and the equivariance and transition clauses of [lem-wf-curve-kummer-jacobian-tate-module]. If $r_n:U_{n+1}\to U_n$ is reduction and $y\in M_{n+1}$, these statements give the explicit compatibility
$$\phi_n(r_nx)(\ell y)=\phi_{n+1}(x)(y)\bmod\ell^n.$$
For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{k}_0/k_0)$, semilinear trace-cup invariance gives
$$\phi_n(\sigma x)(\sigma y)=\phi_n(x)(y),\quad\text{equivalently}\quad
\phi_n(\sigma x)(y)=\phi_n(x)(\sigma^{-1}y).$$
Thus the dual action is the contragredient action, with trivial action on $A_n$. The auxiliary lemma applies to $C/\overline{k}_0$, a smooth proper connected curve over an algebraically closed field, and to its semilinear Galois isomorphisms. It supplies full Galois invariance and coefficient reduction; Frobenius invariance alone would not supply these for arbitrary $k_0$.

source.place: Blueprint proof, claimed equivariance and reduction compatibility before (4.3)

proof.text: Let $T=T_\ell J$ with projections $p_n:T\to M_n$, using the coordinate description of [def-wf-abelian-tate-module]. Divisibility of $J(\overline{k}_0)$ in [thm-av-final](d) implies that $M_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\ell}M_n$ is onto: a lift $z$ of $y$ satisfies $\ell^{n+1}z=\ell^ny=0$. Recursively lifting $y\in M_n$ upwards and setting the lower coordinates to $\ell^{n-j}y$ constructs a tuple with $p_n(t)=y$; hence $p_n$ is onto. Further, $p_n(\ell^nt)=0$. Conversely, if $p_n(t)=0$, put $s_j=t_{j+n}$; then $\ell^js_j=t_n=0$ and $\ell s_{j+1}=s_j$, so $s\in T$ and $\ell^ns=t$. Therefore $\ker p_n=\ell^nT$ and the maps $p_n$ identify $T/\ell^nT$ with $M_n$. All these projections commute with Galois because its action is componentwise.

source.place: Blueprint proof, quotient description following (4.3); direct lifting-and-shift argument in place of compatible bases

proof.text:
For a compatible tuple $x=(x_n)\in\varprojlim U_n$, define
$$F_x(t)=(\phi_n(x_n)(p_nt))_{n\geq1}.$$
Step 2 makes these residues compatible, so this is an element of $\mathbf Z_\ell$, which is the ring of compatible residues in [def-tate-module-abelian-group]. Coordinatewise additivity and scalar multiplication show that $F_x:T\to\mathbf Z_\ell$ is $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear. If $F_x=0$, surjectivity of $p_n$ and injectivity of $\phi_n$ give $x_n=0$ for every $n$; thus $x\mapsto F_x$ is injective.

source.place: Blueprint proof, inverse-limit-to-Hom map; explicit coordinate construction

proof.text: Conversely let $F:T\to\mathbf Z_\ell$ be $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear. By step 3, $F\bmod\ell^n$ kills $\ker p_n=\ell^nT$ and descends uniquely to an $A_n$-linear $f_n:M_n\to A_n$. For $y\in M_{n+1}$ choose $t\in T$ with $p_{n+1}t=y$. Both $f_n(\ell y)$ and $f_{n+1}(y)\bmod\ell^n$ are $F(t)\bmod\ell^n$. Put $x_n=\phi_n^{-1}(f_n)$. Step 2 gives $\phi_n(r_nx_{n+1})(\ell y)=f_n(\ell y)$; surjectivity of $\ell:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ implies $r_nx_{n+1}=x_n$. This tuple maps back to $F$, since every residue of its value on every $t$ agrees with that of $F(t)$. The two constructions are inverse and linear.

source.place: Blueprint proof, final Hom/inverse-limit identification; explicit inverse

proof.text:
Give the dual the action $(\sigma F)(t)=F(\sigma^{-1}t)$. By step 2 and the equivariance of $p_n$ in step 3,
$$F_{\sigma x}(t)_n=\phi_n(\sigma x_n)(p_nt)
=\phi_n(x_n)(\sigma^{-1}p_nt)=F_x(\sigma^{-1}t)_n.$$
Equality of all residues proves Galois equivariance. The isomorphism uses only the canonical cup-trace pairing, Kummer maps and projections; the lifts in step 3 were used only to prove surjectivity. This proves the stated natural isomorphism using ordinary inverse limits.

source.place: Blueprint proof, last paragraph: canonicity and Galois action

lean.note: The additive equivalence is explicitly linear for the usual coordinatewise Z_l action, expressed via residues instead of introducing a new module instance. Equivariance is simultaneous invariance of evaluation under the canonical cohomology pullback and the unique geometric Jacobian action; this is exactly the contragredient dual action. The auxiliary declaration constructs the coefficient-reduction diagram from the existing constant sheaf and cohomology functors.
